newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil firms to sell 6 pct stake in Ericsson unit.
newsitem.headline: Brazil firms to sell 6 pct stake in Ericsson unit.

text.p: Brazil's Monteiro Aranha group and local bank Bradesco hope to rake in 160 million reais ($149.5 million) from the block sale of 2.7 billion preferred shares of Ericsson Telecomunicacoes SA.
"With prices at current levels, we hope to make a premium," Monteiro Aranha Assistant Director Sergio Francisco Guimaraes told Reuters.
The stake, comprised of two billion shares owned by Monteiro Aranha and 700 million shares held by Bradesco, accounts for about six percent of the total capital stock in Ericsson's Brazilian unit.
Ericsson Telecomunicacoes is the Brazilian unit of Sweden's telecom equipment giant Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson, which aims be a major supplier to Brazil's new private telecom operators.
Monteiro Aranha currently holds 3.72 billion preferred shares in Ericsson Telecomunicacoes.
By shedding two billion shares of that stake in the block sale, Monteiro Aranha hopes to raise 118 million reais for investments in other ventures.
"We want to raise cash to invest in cellular phones, electrical energy and water and sewer services," Guimaraes said.
Monteiro Aranha is a member of the Brascom consortium bidding on concessions to operate cellular services on Brazil's B Band frequency, which is now being privatized.
Other members of the consortium are Brazilian construction firm Andrade Gutierrez, Southwestern Bell of the United States and cellular opertor Mannesmann Eurokom of Germany.
The consortium has bid on six B Band concessions of Brazil, including the coveted areas of Sao Paulo city and state, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states and Minas Gerais state.
To promote their sale of Ericsson preferred shares, Monteiro Aranha and Bradesco kicked off a road show in Rio de Janeiro on Thursday.
They were slated to continue it Friday in Sao Paulo.
The offer also would be promoted in the United States and Europe, Guimaraes said.
The shares, which are to be priced June 23 or 24, would be sold locally through a secondary, over-the-counter offering but would be available to foreign investors via Annex IV rules, he said.
Ericsson preferred were off 1.21 percent at 57.30 reais per 1000 shares at midday on the Sao Paulo bourse.
